The law is therefore taken as it stood in April 2018, before the Notaries (Amendment) Acts No. 31 of 2022 and No. 6 of 2024 and before the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Acts No. 30 of 2022 and No. 4 of 2024.
corpus_gaps: Prescribed forms are not in the corpus. Form F 1 of the Second Schedule to the Notaries Ordinance (the list that must accompany the certified copy under rule (29)) cannot be inspected, and rule (29) referred to "the Form F" in April 2018; the words "Form F 1" now shown in the consolidated body were substituted by Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3(9).

Stamp duty on the transfer of immovable property is a devolved Provincial Council levy. The land in this matter is in the Matara District (Southern Province), and the Southern Province finance statute is not in the corpus. The only provincial finance statute present is the Western Province Financial Statute No. 6 of 1990, which by its own s.37 charges duty only on transfers of immovable property situated in the Western Province and therefore does not govern a Matara land transfer.

Text of section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance as it stood before the substitution by Act No. 30 of 2022 s.2.

Text of section 34 of the Notaries Ordinance as it stood before the substitution by Act No. 31 of 2022 s.17, and the First and Second Schedules to the Increase of Fines Act No. 12 of 2005, which together would give the April 2018 penalty for a breach of a rule in section 31.

The Constitution of Sri Lanka is not in the corpus. Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006 s.9 turns on "documents and instruments referred to in List I of the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution" and on the Provinces "set out in the Eighth Schedule"; neither Schedule can be read from the corpus, so the devolution premise behind s.9 cannot be verified here.

The Notaries Ordinance text in the corpus is a consolidation carrying the 2022 and 2024 amendments. Rule (7A) of s.31 (notary to pay the stamp duty and affix the bank receipt) was inserted by Act No. 31 of 2022 and amended by Act No. 6 of 2024, and rule (30A) (registration within thirty days) was inserted in 2022; neither was in force in April 2018 and neither has been relied on. Rule (26) of s.31 is shown in the consolidated body without its rule number and is recorded in the corpus as repealed by Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(12), yet its text is still carried in the consolidated body - the verifier should treat the numbering of that rule as a corpus artefact.

The pre-2022 text of Notaries Ordinance s.34 is not in the corpus. Section 34 was replaced by Act No. 31 of 2022 s.17, so the fine applicable in April 2018 to a breach of a s.31 rule cannot be stated from the corpus.

The rate of stamp duty on a deed transferring immovable property is not in the corpus. Stamp Duty Act No. 43 of 1982 s.2 charges duty "at the prescribed rate" and s.69 leaves the rate to regulations; Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006 s.3 leaves it to a Ministerial Order published in the Gazette. No rate order, regulation or rate schedule has been extracted into the corpus, so the money figure for a Rs.1,000,000 transfer cannot be derived from the corpus.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument in any area other than that in which he is authorized to practice, nor in any language other than that in which he is authorized to practice nor authenticate or attest any deed or instrument drawn in any language other than that in which he is authorized to practice.
provisions.why_relevant: This is the only rule in section 31 that limits where a notary may attest. It restricts the area in which the act of attestation is performed and the language of the deed; it says nothing about where the land affected by the deed is situated. It is therefore the provision that answers how Lal Peiris, whose warrant covers Colombo, may lawfully attest a deed relating to land at Matara.
provisions.temporal_note: Rule (22) is part of the original 1907 rules. It is not among the rules substituted, inserted or repealed by the amendments recorded against section 31 (Act No. 20 of 1976, Act No. 47 of 2011, Act No. 31 of 2022, Act No. 6 of 2024), so the text quoted stood in this form in April 2018.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: Every warrant issued to a notary under the provisions of section 3* or section 4* authorizing him to practice as a notary in any judicial division in which he resides, shall be deemed to authorize him to practice as a notary in the judicial zone in which he resides.
provisions.why_relevant: Fixes the extent of the "area ... in which he is authorized to practice" for the purposes of rule (22) of section 31. Without it the area is read as the judicial division named in the warrant; with it the notary may attest anywhere in the judicial zone in which he resides. It is the provision that tells us how far Lal Peiris's Colombo authority reaches.
provisions.temporal_note: Inserted by the Notaries (Amendment) Law No. 20 of 1976 s.4 and in force from 1976. No later amendment is recorded against it, so it was in force in April 2018.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: Every notary shall be bound to have his office within the area specified in his warrant
provisions.why_relevant: Explains why Lal Peiris's office is in Colombo and anchors the area of his warrant. It is background: it constrains where he keeps his office, not what deeds he may attest.
provisions.temporal_note: Original 1907 text; no amendment recorded against section 9. In force in April 2018.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument to which he is a party.
provisions.why_relevant: The scenario stresses that the purchaser is a friend of the notary. Rule (13) is the only disqualification in section 31 based on the notary's own connection with the deed, and it is confined to his being a party. It is needed to show that friendship with an executant is not a statutory bar to attestation.
provisions.temporal_note: Original 1907 rule; not among the rules amended by Act No. 47 of 2011, Act No. 31 of 2022 or Act No. 6 of 2024. In force in this form in April 2018.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: No sale, purchase, transfer, assignment, or mortgage of land or other immovable property, and no promise, bargain, contract, or agreement for effecting any such object
provisions.why_relevant: Supplies the reason a notary must attest at all: a sale or transfer of immovable property is of no force in law unless the deed is in writing and attested by a licensed notary. It frames the question of how Lal Peiris may attest this particular deed of transfer.
provisions.temporal_note: The opening words quoted are original 1840 text and stood in this form in April 2018. The detailed conditions in paragraphs (a) and (b) of subsection (1) and the whole of subsection (2), as they appear in the corpus consolidation, reflect the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Acts No. 30 of 2022 and No. 4 of 2024 and are NOT the April 2018 text; nothing in this map relies on them.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument, other than a will or codicil, affecting land or other immovable property, unless the deed or instrument embodies therin or in a Schedule annexed therto an accurate and clear description of the said land or other property affected thereby, showing its boundaries, extent, situation specifying the district
provisions.why_relevant: Requires the deed itself to state the district in which the land is situated. That statement is what makes the Matara District identifiable on the face of the deed, which is the trigger for the out-of-district duty in rule (29) and part of what Lal Peiris must do before he can attest.
provisions.temporal_note: Paragraph (a) of rule (16) was substituted by the Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 47 of 2011 s.2, in force well before April 2018. It applies precisely where a deed other than a will or codicil affects land in a district other than that in which the attesting notary resides, which is this case: the notary resides in Colombo, the land is in Matara. It fixes both the act required (a certified copy plus a list in duplicate, signed by him) and the deadline (the fifteenth day of the following month).

provisions.why_relevant: Links the notary's attestation duty to stamp duty: he may not attest until he is assured the duty is provided. It is why the stamp duty questions arise for Lal Peiris at all, and it is part of what he must satisfy before attesting.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: All stamp duty payable to a Provincial Council in respect of documents and instruments referred to in List I of the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution, shall be paid to the respective Provincial Council within whose limits the instrument was executed or the property situated as the case may be
provisions.why_relevant: The only provision in the corpus that addresses where stamp duty is to be paid when the duty is a Provincial Council levy. It is the starting point for question 4, but it is also the source of the difficulty: it offers two limbs, the place of execution and the place where the property is situated, and leaves the choice between them to be resolved "as the case may be" by reference to List I of the Ninth Schedule, which is not in the corpus.
provisions.temporal_note: Original 2006 text; no amendment recorded against section 9. In force in April 2018.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: The stamp duty with which any instrument is chargeable shall be paid before or at the time of execution of the instrument and such payment shall be indicated on such instrument by means of adhesive stamps or impressed stamps except as otherwise permitted in this Act.
provisions.why_relevant: Gives the time and the manner of payment under the 1982 Act: before or at execution, evidenced by adhesive or impressed stamps on the instrument. It is the part of the "where and how" of payment that the corpus does answer, and it is what the notary must see satisfied before he attests.
provisions.temporal_note: Original 1982 text; no amendment recorded against section 6. In force in April 2018. Note that the 1982 Act contains no provision equivalent to the prescribed-bank machinery found in provincial finance statutes, so the identity of the office or bank that receives the money for a Southern Province land transfer cannot be established from this section alone.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: He shall not authenticate or attest any deed or instrument unless the person executing the same and the witnesses shall have signed the same in his presence and in the presence of one another, and unless he shall have signed the same in the presence of the executant and of the attesting witnesses.

The Q01 answer concludes that the parties and the two witnesses must execute the deed before Lal Peiris at his Colombo office, but no provision in the map stated that requirement: rule (22) fixes only the area and the language, and rule (16)(a) only the description of the land. Rule (12) is the provision that requires execution in the notary's presence and in the presence of one another, and it is what ties the place of signing to the place of attestation on which rule (22) operates.

It is not among the rules amended by Notaries (Amendment) Law No. 20 of 1976 s.10 (rules (29) and (36)(b)), Act No. 47 of 2011 ss.2-3 (rule (16)(a) and rule (26)), Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16 or Act No. 6 of 2024 s.3, each of which enumerates the rules it touches. questions.authority_requirement_reason: Whether a notary may attest a deed relating to land lying outside the area of his warrant is settled by rule (22) of section 31 of the Notaries Ordinance read with section 4A, which together define the area within which he may attest. Whether his friendship with the purchaser disqualifies him is settled by rule (13), which confines the disqualification to being a party. The requirement of notarial attestation for a transfer of immovable property comes from section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance. No judicial authority or Roman-Dutch doctrine is needed to reach a complete answer.

legal_issues.issue: Whether the area restriction on a notary's practice bars a Colombo notary from attesting a deed of transfer of land situated in the Matara District, or whether it restricts only the place at which the act of attestation is performed.
How far the warrant of a notary who resides in Colombo extends, and what counts as the area in which he is authorised to practise.
Whether the notary's friendship with the purchaser disqualifies him from attesting the deed.
What the notary must do on the face of the deed, in particular as to language and the description of the land, in order to attest it lawfully.

questions.hop_count_basis: One directly applicable rule, rule (22) of section 31, plus one necessary linked provision, section 4A, which fixes the extent of the "area in which he is authorized to practice" on which rule (22) turns. Rule (13) is a second first-order rule on the same facts rather than a further link in the chain, so it does not add a hop. Counting only the indispensable dependencies gives two hops.

enrichment.original_background: Lal Peiris is a Notary practicing in Colombo. Waruna Liyanage a friend of Lal Peiris wishes to purchase a house and property in Matara and wants it to be attested by Lal Peiris. The market value of the property is Rs.1,000,000/-
enrichment.enriched_background: Lal Peiris is a Notary practicing in Colombo. Waruna Liyanage a friend of Lal Peiris wishes to purchase a house and property in Matara and wants it to be attested by Lal Peiris. The market value of the property is Rs.1,000,000/-. Lal Peiris holds a notarial warrant authorising him to practise as a notary in the Sinhala language in the judicial division in which he resides, Colombo, and he lives and keeps his only notarial office at No. 42, Barnes Place, Colombo 07. The property Waruna Liyanage is buying is Lot 3 in Survey Plan No. 2214 dated 4 January 2016, fifteen perches in extent with a two-storeyed dwelling house standing on it, at Kumbalwella within the Matara Four Gravets in the Matara District of the Southern Province; the vendor is Nimal Wickramasinghe of Matara, who holds a clear paper title. The deed of transfer is drawn in Sinhala, and Nimal Wickramasinghe, Waruna Liyanage and two witnesses have arranged to come to Lal Peiris's Colombo office and to sign it there together, in one another's presence and in the presence of Lal Peiris, on 12 March 2018. Lal Peiris is neither the vendor nor the purchaser, takes nothing under the deed and has no interest of any kind in the Matara property; his only connection with the transaction is his friendship with Waruna Liyanage. Waruna Liyanage has told Lal Peiris that he will put him in funds for the stamps before the day of signing.

Rule (22) turns on the area and the language in which he is authorised to practise, and section 4A turns on the judicial division in which he resides, so the warrant's terms and his place of residence have to be stated before the rule can be applied.

gold_answer_draft.issue: Whether Lal Peiris, a notary whose warrant authorises him to practise in Colombo and who is a friend of the purchaser, may attest a deed transferring land situated in the Matara District, and what he must do in order to attest it lawfully.
gold_answer_draft.rule: A transfer of immovable property is of no force in law unless the deed is in writing and attested by a licensed notary (Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2). The area limit on a notary is imposed by Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (22), which forbids him to authenticate or attest any deed "in any area other than that in which he is authorized to practice", and to attest in, or to attest a deed drawn in, a language other than that in which he is authorised to practise. The restriction is on the place at which the notary performs the attestation and on the language of the deed; rule (22) says nothing about where the land affected by the deed is situated. The area in which he is authorised to practise is fixed by his warrant, extended by Notaries Ordinance s.4A, under which a warrant authorising practice in the judicial division in which he resides is deemed to authorise practice in the judicial zone in which he resides; s.9 requires him to keep his office within the area specified in the warrant. The only disqualification in s.31 arising from the notary's own relationship to the deed is rule (13), which forbids him to attest a deed to which he is a party. Before attesting, he must have an assurance that the required stamp duty is provided (s.31 rule (6)), and the deed must embody an accurate and clear description of the land showing its boundaries, extent and situation, specifying the district (s.31 rule (16)(a)).
gold_answer_draft.application: Lal Peiris's warrant authorises him to practise in the Sinhala language in Colombo, the judicial division in which he resides, and by s.4A that authority extends to the Colombo judicial zone. The deed is drawn in Sinhala, and the vendor, the purchaser and the two witnesses are to sign it together in his presence at his Colombo office on 12 March 2018. The act of attestation is therefore performed within the area and in the language in which he is authorised to practise, and rule (22) is satisfied. That the land lies at Kumbalwella in the Matara District does not engage rule (22), because that rule looks to the area in which the notary acts and not to the situation of the land; the Matara District instead has to be stated in the description of the land under rule (16)(a). Lal Peiris is not the vendor or the purchaser, takes nothing under the deed and has no interest in the property, so rule (13) is not engaged; his friendship with Waruna Liyanage is not a matter on which s.31 fastens. He must also satisfy himself under rule (6) that the stamp duty is provided, and Waruna Liyanage has undertaken to put him in funds before the day of signing.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: Lal Peiris may attest the deed. He must do so within the Colombo judicial zone, which his warrant covers by virtue of Notaries Ordinance s.4A, and in the language in which he is authorised to practise, so the parties and the two witnesses must execute the deed before him at his Colombo office and not at Matara (s.31 rule (22)). The situation of the land at Matara is no bar to his attesting; it must, however, be described in the deed with its district under s.31 rule (16)(a), and he must not attest until he has an assurance that the stamp duty is provided (s.31 rule (6)). His friendship with the purchaser does not disqualify him, since he is not a party to the deed (s.31 rule (13)).

answer_claims.claim_text: A sale or transfer of immovable property is of no force in law unless the deed is in writing and attested by a licensed notary.

A notary may not authenticate or attest any deed in an area other than that in which he is authorised to practise, nor in, nor of a deed drawn in, a language other than that in which he is authorised to practise.

The area restriction in rule (22) attaches to the place at which the notary performs the attestation and to the language of the deed, and not to the district in which the land affected by the deed is situated.
A warrant authorising a notary to practise in the judicial division in which he resides is deemed to authorise him to practise in the judicial zone in which he resides.
The only disqualification in section 31 based on the notary's own connection with the deed is rule (13), which bars him from attesting a deed to which he is a party.

A notary may not attest a deed affecting land unless the deed embodies an accurate and clear description of the land showing its boundaries, extent and situation, specifying the district, and may not attest unless he has an assurance that the required stamp duty is provided.

Lal Peiris's warrant covers the Colombo judicial division in which he resides and therefore the Colombo judicial zone, and the deed is to be executed before him in Sinhala at his Colombo office, so the attestation takes place within the area and in the language in which he is authorised to practise.
The situation of the land at Kumbalwella in the Matara District does not engage rule (22); it engages instead the requirement that the deed describe the land and specify its district.
Lal Peiris is not a party to the deed and takes no benefit under it, so rule (13) is not engaged and his friendship with the purchaser is not a statutory disqualification.

Lal Peiris may attest the deed, provided the parties and the two witnesses execute it before him within the Colombo judicial zone and in a language in which he is authorised to practise, the deed describes the Matara land with its district, and he has an assurance that the stamp duty is provided.
If Lal Peiris were instead to attest the deed at Matara, he would be attesting in an area other than that in which he is authorised to practise and would breach rule (22).

gold_answer_draft.rule: Every notary must, under Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (26)(a)(i), deliver or transmit to the Registrar of Lands of the district in which he resides, so as to reach the registrar on or before the fifteenth day of every month, the duplicate of every deed or instrument (except wills and codicils) executed or acknowledged before or attested by him during the preceding month, together with a list in duplicate signed by him in the prescribed form. Where the deed is one other than a will or codicil and affects land situated in a district other than that in which the attesting notary resides, s.31 rule (29) casts an additional duty on him: on or before the fifteenth day of the month next following that in which the deed was executed, and besides transmitting the duplicate in the manner already described, he must deliver or transmit to the Registrar of Lands of the district in which the land is situated a copy of the deed certified by him as correct, together with a list in duplicate in the prescribed form signed by him of all such deeds as relate to lands in that district. The district of the land is the district which s.31 rule (16)(a) requires to be specified in the description of the land in the deed itself. Breach of a rule set out in s.31 is an offence punishable on summary trial before a Magistrate, in addition to any civil liability the notary incurs (s.34).
gold_answer_draft.application: Lal Peiris resides in the Colombo District and attests the deed at his Colombo office on 12 March 2018. The deed is an ordinary deed of transfer, not a will or codicil, and he is the only notary before whom it is executed, so the duty of transmitting the duplicate rests on him. The land conveyed is at Kumbalwella in the Matara District, a district other than the Colombo District in which he resides, so s.31 rule (29) is engaged. His ordinary duty under rule (26)(a)(i) is to send the duplicate of the deed, with the signed list in duplicate, to the Registrar of Lands, Colombo, so as to reach that registrar on or before 15 April 2018. Rule (29) then requires him, in addition and by the same date of 15 April 2018, to deliver or transmit to the Registrar of Lands, Matara, a copy of the deed certified by him as correct, together with a list in duplicate signed by him of the deeds he has attested that relate to lands in the Matara District. The deed must in any event describe the land as being in the Matara District under rule (16)(a), which is what identifies the registrar to whom the certified copy must go.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: Because the land lies in the Matara District and Lal Peiris resides in the Colombo District, s.31 rule (29) of the Notaries Ordinance casts on him the additional duty of delivering or transmitting to the Registrar of Lands, Matara, on or before the fifteenth day of the month next following execution, that is on or before 15 April 2018 for a deed executed on 12 March 2018, a copy of the deed certified by him as correct together with a list in duplicate in the prescribed form signed by him of the deeds relating to lands in that district. This is over and above, and does not replace, his ordinary duty under s.31 rule (26)(a)(i) to transmit the duplicate and his monthly list to the Registrar of Lands, Colombo, by the same date. Failure to observe the rule is an offence under s.34 of the Ordinance in addition to any civil liability he may incur; the fine applicable in April 2018 cannot be stated from the corpus, which carries only the later text of s.34.

answer_claims.claim_text: A notary must deliver or transmit to the Registrar of Lands of the district in which he resides, so as to reach the registrar on or before the fifteenth day of every month, the duplicate of every deed or instrument except wills and codicils executed or acknowledged before or attested by him during the preceding month.

Where a deed other than a will or codicil affects land in a district other than that in which the attesting notary resides, he must, on or before the fifteenth day of the month next following that in which the deed was executed and besides transmitting the duplicate as already required, deliver or transmit to the Registrar of Lands of the district in which the land is situated a copy of the deed certified by him as correct, with a signed list in duplicate of the deeds relating to lands in that district.
The rule (29) duty is additional to and not in substitution for the ordinary monthly duty, because it operates besides transmitting the duplicate in the manner already required.
The district in which the land is situated is the district that the deed itself must specify in its description of the land.
Breach of a rule set out in section 31 makes the notary guilty of an offence triable summarily before a Magistrate, in addition to any civil liability he may incur.

Lal Peiris resides in the Colombo District while the land conveyed is at Kumbalwella in the Matara District, so the deed affects land in a district other than that in which he resides and rule (29) is engaged.
The instrument is a deed of transfer and not a will or codicil, and Lal Peiris is the only notary attesting it, so the duty of transmission falls on him.

The deed having been executed on 12 March 2018, both the duplicate to the Registrar of Lands, Colombo and the certified copy to the Registrar of Lands, Matara must reach or be transmitted by 15 April 2018.

The duty cast on Lal Peiris is to deliver or transmit to the Registrar of Lands, Matara, on or before 15 April 2018, a copy of the deed certified by him as correct together with a list in duplicate signed by him of the deeds relating to lands in the Matara District, in addition to sending the duplicate and his monthly list to the Registrar of Lands, Colombo by the same date.

If he fails to observe that duty he commits an offence under section 34 of the Notaries Ordinance in addition to any civil liability, though the fine applicable in April 2018 cannot be stated from the corpus.

gold_answer_draft.issue: What amount of stamp duty is payable on a deed transferring immovable property in the Matara District where the value of the property conveyed is Rs.1,000,000.
gold_answer_draft.rule: Stamp duty is charged on every instrument executed, drawn or presented in Sri Lanka "at the prescribed rate", and different rates may be prescribed for different classes of instruments (Stamp Duty Act No. 43 of 1982 s.2). Although the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006 displaced much of the 1982 Act, s.13 of the 2006 Act expressly excepts any instrument relating to the transfer of immovable property, so the 1982 Act continues to govern a deed of transfer of land. Where property is conveyed by an instrument, the duty is calculated on the value of the property conveyed, without deduction for any mortgage, encumbrance or reservation of interest (s.15 of the 1982 Act). Except where there is an agreement to the contrary, the duty on a conveyance is payable by the grantee (s.24(b)). A notary may not attest until he has an assurance that the required stamp duty is provided (Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (6)).
gold_answer_draft.application: The deed is an outright transfer of Lot 3 at Kumbalwella in the Matara District, immovable property, so by s.13 of the 2006 Act the 1982 Act governs it. Under s.15(1) the duty falls to be calculated on the value of the property conveyed, which on 12 March 2018 was Rs.1,000,000, the stated consideration being the same figure; nothing is deducted, the property passing free of encumbrance. There being no agreement to the contrary, s.24(b) makes the duty payable by Waruna Liyanage as grantee, and Lal Peiris may not attest until he is assured that it is provided. What cannot be taken from the corpus is the last step. Section 2 charges duty only "at the prescribed rate" and leaves the rate to be prescribed; no rate order, regulation or rate schedule for a transfer of immovable property has been extracted into the corpus. Stamp duty on the transfer of immovable property is in any event a devolved provincial levy, and the finance statute of the Southern Province, in which the Matara District lies, is not in the corpus either. The only provincial finance statute present is that of the Western Province, and by its own s.37 it charges duty only on transfers of property situated in the Western Province, so it cannot supply the rate for a Matara land.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The base is established but the rate is not. On the facts the duty is calculated on Rs.1,000,000, the value of the property conveyed, and is payable by Waruna Liyanage as grantee; but the money figure cannot be stated from the corpus, because Stamp Duty Act No. 43 of 1982 s.2 charges duty at a rate that has to be prescribed by subordinate legislation, and neither that subordinate legislation nor the Southern Province finance statute governing a Matara land transfer is in the corpus. This question is therefore recorded as blocked for missing authority rather than answered with a figure.

gold_answer_draft.issue: To whom, and by what means, Lal Peiris is to pay the stamp duty on a deed of transfer executed in Colombo in respect of land situated in the Matara District.
gold_answer_draft.rule: Because the instrument relates to the transfer of immovable property, it falls within the exception in s.13 of the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006 and remains governed by the Stamp Duty Act No. 43 of 1982. Section 9 of the 2006 Act provides that all stamp duty payable to a Provincial Council in respect of documents and instruments referred to in List I of the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution shall be paid to the respective Provincial Council within whose limits the instrument was executed or the property is situated, as the case may be; where the Council for a Province stands dissolved, the duty is paid instead to a bank prescribed by the Commissioner-General until a Council is established for that Province. Under s.6(1) of the 1982 Act the duty must be paid before or at the time of execution of the instrument and the payment must be indicated on the instrument by adhesive or impressed stamps, except as otherwise permitted by that Act; where it is not practicable to use stamps, s.6(3) allows the Commissioner-General to endorse the instrument on payment to him. The duty is payable by the grantee absent an agreement to the contrary (s.24(b)), and the notary may not attest until he has an assurance that it is provided (Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (6)).
gold_answer_draft.application: The deed is executed at Colombo, within the limits of the Western Provincial Council, but the land conveyed lies at Matara, within the limits of the Southern Provincial Council, and both Councils were functioning on 12 March 2018 so the proviso to s.9 is not engaged. Section 9 therefore points to "the respective Provincial Council within whose limits the instrument was executed or the property situated as the case may be", and on these facts the two limbs point to different Councils. Resolving which limb governs a transfer of immovable property requires List I of the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution, to which s.9 expressly refers and which is not in the corpus, and the finance statute of the Southern Province, which is not in the corpus either; the Western Province Financial Statute No. 6 of 1990 is present but by its s.37 charges duty only on transfers of property situated in the Western Province, so it cannot be applied to Matara land. What the corpus does settle is the manner and time of payment: the money must be provided by Waruna Liyanage as grantee, must be paid before or at the time of execution, and the payment must appear on the deed itself by way of adhesive or impressed stamps, with Lal Peiris declining to attest until he is assured that it has been provided.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The corpus establishes that the duty is a Provincial Council levy directed by s.9 of the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006 to the respective Provincial Council within whose limits the instrument was executed or the property is situated, that it must be paid before or at the time of execution and shown on the deed by adhesive or impressed stamps under s.6 of the Stamp Duty Act No. 43 of 1982, and that the grantee provides the money. It does not settle which of the two limbs of s.9 governs a transfer of immovable property executed in one province in respect of land in another, because that turns on List I of the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution and on the Southern Province finance statute, neither of which is in the corpus. The question is therefore recorded as blocked for missing authority rather than answered by choosing a Council.

answer_claims.claim_text: An instrument relating to the transfer of immovable property is excepted from the displacement effected by the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006 and remains governed by the Stamp Duty Act No. 43 of 1982.

All stamp duty payable to a Provincial Council in respect of documents and instruments referred to in List I of the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution is to be paid to the respective Provincial Council within whose limits the instrument was executed or the property is situated, as the case may be.
Where the Provincial Council for a Province stands dissolved, the duty is paid instead to a bank prescribed by the Commissioner-General until a Council is established for that Province.

The duty must be paid before or at the time of execution of the instrument and the payment must be indicated on the instrument by adhesive or impressed stamps, the duty being payable by the grantee absent an agreement to the contrary, and the notary may not attest until assured that it is provided.
The deed is executed within the limits of one Provincial Council and the land lies within the limits of another, so the two limbs of section 9 point to different Councils on these facts.
Both Councils being constituted and functioning on the date of execution, the proviso diverting payment to a prescribed bank is not engaged.
Waruna Liyanage as grantee provides the money before execution, so the duty can be paid and shown on the deed by stamps before or at the time it is signed on 12 March 2018.

The duty is a Provincial Council levy that must be paid before or at execution and evidenced by stamps on the deed, but which of the two limbs of section 9 selects the Council cannot be resolved from the corpus, so the question is blocked for missing authority.

questions.block_reason: Section 9 of the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006 offers two limbs, the Provincial Council within whose limits the instrument was executed and the Council within whose limits the property is situated, and leaves the choice to be made "as the case may be" by reference to List I of the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution. The Constitution is not in the corpus, so the devolved item that would select the limb cannot be read. The finance statute of the Southern Province, in which the Matara land lies and which would identify the receiving office or prescribed bank, is also absent; the only provincial finance statute in the corpus, the Western Province Financial Statute No. 6 of 1990, charges duty by its s.37 only on transfers of property situated in the Western Province and cannot be applied here. The manner and time of payment are established from the corpus, but the identity of the recipient is not.
